variants.query: What is the right of private defence under Section 34?

original.text: Nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence. Right of private defence of body and of property.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 3: GENERAL EXCEPTIONS
Section 34: Things done in private defence.
Nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence. Right of private defence of body and of property.

original.text: If in the exercise of the right of private defence against an assault which reasonably causes the apprehension of death, the defender be so situated that he cannot effectually exercise that right without risk of harm to an innocent person, his right of private defence extends to the running of that risk.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 3: GENERAL EXCEPTIONS
Section 44: Right of private defence against deadly assault when there is risk of harm to innocent person.
If in the exercise of the right of private defence against an assault which reasonably causes the apprehension of death, the defender be so situated that he cannot effectually exercise that right without risk of harm to an innocent person, his right of private defence extends to the running of that risk.

original.text: The right of private defence of the body commences as soon as a reasonable apprehension of danger to the body arises from an attempt or threat to commit the offence though the offence may not have been committed; and it continues as long as such apprehension of danger to the body continues. When right of private defence of property extends to causing death.
original.derived_context:

Chapter 3: GENERAL EXCEPTIONS
Section 40: Commencement and continuance of right of private defence of body.
The right of private defence of the body commences as soon as a reasonable apprehension of danger to the body arises from an attempt or threat to commit the offence though the offence may not have been committed; and it continues as long as such apprehension of danger to the body continues. When right of private defence of property extends to causing death.

original.text: Every person has a right, subject to the restrictions contained in section 37, to defend—

Chapter 3: GENERAL EXCEPTIONS
Section 35: Right of private defence of body and of property.
Every person has a right, subject to the restrictions contained in section 37, to defend—

original.text: The right of private defence of property extends, under the restrictions specified in section 37, to the voluntary causing of death or of any other harm to the wrong-doer, if the offence, the committing of which, or the attempting to commit which, occasions the exercise of the right, be an offence of any of the descriptions hereinafter enumerated, namely:—

Chapter 3: GENERAL EXCEPTIONS
Section 41: When right of private defence of property extends to causing death.
The right of private defence of property extends, under the restrictions specified in section 37, to the voluntary causing of death or of any other harm to the wrong-doer, if the offence, the committing of which, or the attempting to commit which, occasions the exercise of the right, be an offence of any of the descriptions hereinafter enumerated, namely:—

original.text: A person is not deprived of the right of private defence against an act done, or attempted to be done, by the direction of a public servant, unless he knows, or has reason to believe, that the person doing the act is acting by such direction, or unless such person states the authority under which he acts, or if he has authority in writing, unless he produces such authority, if demanded. phase11.final_answer: The right of private defence under Section 34 allows individuals to act in self-defense without it being considered an offence, specifically for the protection of body and property.
phase11.summary_answer: The right of private defence under Section 34 allows individuals to act in self-defense without it being considered an offence, specifically for the protection of body and property.
phase11.detailed_answer: Under Section 34 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, nothing is considered an offence if it is done in the exercise of the right of private defence. This right applies to both the defence of one's body and property. The right of private defence commences when there is a reasonable apprehension of danger and continues as long as that apprehension exists. Additionally, the right extends to situations where the defender may risk harm to an innocent person while exercising this right (Section 44). Furthermore, the right of private defence of property can include the voluntary causing of death or harm to a wrong-doer under certain conditions (Section 41).
